ImageDescription.value: Worker home from 1911 in Helsinki as preserved in the Worker Housing Museum. This typical one-room apartment was home to Aksel, a diver for the City of Helsinki, and his wife Alviina who probably did domestic work in upper class households. They had no children but it was very common to have large families living in such small homes.

ImageDescription.value: Worker home from 1927 in Helsinki as preserved in the Worker Housing Museum. This typical one-room apartment was home to Kaarle, a retired carpenter, his wife Anna-Liisa and their adult daughter Ida and also adult granddaughters Alina and Lyyli, all workers. Multigenerational living and large families in such small homes was typical for the period.
